title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from this page and pp. 63 and 65. E and E' are sets, each with a relation written x|o|y. The note on p. 65 records that symmetry is used. The relation extends to subsets: A|o|B means every element of A is |o| to every element of B. The operator s-pr°_E (the machine transcription has supp°; the image reads 's-pr°' / 'sup-pr°') is the double polar for this relation. The test is: B ⊂ s-pr°(A) iff every x with x|o|A also satisfies x|o|B. So s-pr°(A) = A^{⊥⊥}, a closure operator (monotone, extensive, idempotent) coming from the polarity of a symmetric relation. Σ_E is then the complete lattice of closed subsets, i.e. the ortholattice-like structure of an orthogonality space.

A correspondence α: E → P(E') extends to subsets by ᾱ(A) = ∪_{x∈A} α(x). It induces α_*: Σ_E → Σ_E', sending a closed set S to s-pr°_E'(ᾱ(S)).

On p. 63 Grothendieck chose an optimal 'transpose' α*(x') = {x : α(x) ⊂ s-pr°_E'({x'})}. He imposed two conditions:
(i) s-pr°_E'(ᾱ(α*(x'))) = s-pr°_E'({x'});
(ii) 'faithful compatibility': x|o|y ⇔ ᾱ(x)|o|ᾱ(y).

This page opens by noting that these conditions give, for subsets, ᾱ(A)|o|ᾱ(B) ⇔ A|o|B. The fragmentary word 'injectif' perhaps refers to α being forced injective. He then worries that the conditions give what is needed 'but perhaps a bit too much'. He asks whether they would force α_*: Σ_E → Σ_E' to be bijective.

Next he wants the formula of p. 59 — or its failure — understood in cases like an earlier example, and admits: 'je n'ai pas l'impression encore d'avoir vraiment bien compris la situation.' He restarts from the formula of p. 59:
 α_*(s-pr°_E(A)) = s-pr°_E'(ᾱ(A)),
where by definition the left side is s-pr°_E'(ᾱ(s-pr°_E(A))).

The inclusion ⊃ is clear: A ⊂ s-pr°_E(A) gives ᾱ(A) ⊂ ᾱ(s-pr°_E(A)), and one applies the monotone closure s-pr°_E'. The problem is therefore the inclusion ⊂, equivalently ᾱ(cl A) ⊂ cl(ᾱ A), a 'continuity' of α for the two closure operators.

On p. 65 this is solved by requiring an adjoint correspondence β: E' → P(E) with x|o|β(x') ⇔ α(x)|o|x'. This is the standard condition making the induced map of closed-set lattices well behaved (adjointable maps of orthosets; morphisms of polarity contexts). The overall aim is functoriality of the closed-set lattice Σ under correspondences, part of an exploratory 'dispositions' formalism in the 1986 Ateliers notes.
errors: The passage from (ii) to the subset statement ᾱ(A)|o|ᾱ(B) ⇔ A|o|B is immediate from the pointwise definition of |o| on subsets. No injectivity is needed for it; any injectivity conclusion would require extra hypotheses, e.g. irreflexivity and separation of the relation.

No mathematical error on the page. The argument for ⊃ is correct and the reverse inclusion is correctly isolated as the real problem. The page is openly exploratory: Grothendieck says he has not understood the situation.

ideas.what: Closure s-pr° = double polar of a symmetric relation |o| on a set; Σ_E = lattice of closed sets
ideas.modern_name: Polarity / Galois connection closure; orthogonality space (orthoset) and its lattice of orthoclosed subsets

ideas.what: Correspondence α: E → P(E') inducing α_*: Σ_E → Σ_E' via closure of the image; question whether α_* commutes with closure
ideas.modern_name: Continuity of a map for closure operators; morphisms of orthosets / formal contexts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard closure-space theory; Paseka–Vetterlein on categories of orthosets (2020s)

ideas.what: Faithful compatibility: x|o|y ⇔ ᾱ(x)|o|ᾱ(y), and the question whether it forces α_* bijective
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orthoset / quantum-logic literature (Wigner-type theorems, Vetterlein et al.)

missed.claim: Across pp. 63–65 Grothendieck builds what is essentially the category of orthogonality spaces with adjointable correspondences: the condition x|o|β(x') ⇔ α(x)|o|x' and an optimal adjoint. This is the Chu-space morphism / Barwise–Seligman infomorphism condition specialised to a symmetric relation. The present page isolates when the induced lattice map commutes with closure.
missed.quote: Donc la formule (cf. p. 59) α_* s-pr°_E(A) = s-pr°_E'(ᾱ(A)) ... l'inclusion ⊃ est claire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents Grothendieck in 1986 independently arriving at the orthoset / Chu / formal-concept morphism framework. That is of mild interest for biographies of the 'dispositions' / Ateliers material, not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine closure-operator and polarity reasoning in an exploratory, self-doubting mode. The only interest is that it fits an independent rediscovery of adjointable morphisms of orthogonality spaces (Chu-type morphisms), which is well established elsewhere.
transcription_corrections: The page number at the top is 64 (archive p. 67), not 68.
The operator is 's-pr°' / 'sup-pr°' (as on pp. 63 and 65), not 'supp°'.

The bracket under the formula: the left side α_*(s-pr°_E(A)) is equal by definition to s-pr°_E'(ᾱ(s-pr°_E(A))). 'α_*' is overwritten rather than deleted, and the right side is s-pr°_E'(ᾱ(A)) with the A overwritten.
Probable reading: 'Ces conditions ... donnent ce qu'il nous faut, mais peut-être même un peu [-plus-] trop'.
Probable reading: 'par exemple α_*: Σ_E ⥲ Σ_E' bijectif ?' — the subscript is E (a struck-through letter corrected to E).
Probable reading: 'Donc je n'ai pas l'impression encore d'avoir vraiment bien compris la situation.'
Last lines: 'puisque s-pr°_E(A) ⊃ A d'où ᾱ(s-pr°_E(A)) ⊃ ᾱ(A) et il suffit de passer aux s-pr°_E'. Donc le pb est'.
